transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because it’s been going on for months, and I feel like every time I try to explain it, people act like I’m making connections that aren’t there, but I’m not. My husband’s family has been quietly interfering with our money and our reputation—our good name, really—and it shows up in these little ways that people keep brushing off.

Like, I work in billing, so I know what a normal error looks like, and lately there have been these small billing mistakes or things that just don’t sit right, and people say, “Oh, it’s just a clerical thing,” but I can tell when something is being nudged along. And then at church someone will suddenly act strange toward me, like they heard something or they’re looking at me differently, and I’m supposed to pretend that’s nothing too.

Everyone keeps saying, “Well, the records don’t show that,” or “We pulled this up and it looks fine,” but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a trail behind it. I know it ties back to his family. They’re not doing it in some obvious way where anyone can just point to one big thing. It’s quiet, it’s spread out, and that’s what makes it so hard to get people to understand.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that others around you don't seem to notice or hear?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal things—people talking in another room, noises outside, the phone, that kind of thing—but not voices that nobody else hears, if that’s what you mean.

And I haven’t seen, like… things that aren’t there. It’s more that I notice how people act or the timing of things, but I’m not seeing visions or hearing some voice telling me things. That’s not what’s happening.

Aside from this situation with your husband's family, have you generally had a long-standing pattern—going back to your teens or twenties—of finding it hard to trust people or suspecting that others are trying to deceive or harm you in other areas of your life?

I don’t know that I’d say it goes all the way back like that. I mean, I’ve never been the kind of person who just tells everybody my business, but I don’t think that’s the same as thinking everyone is out to get me.

When I was younger, I had normal worries, I guess—like whether someone was being honest, or whether a friend was really a friend—but I don’t remember it being this… this constant thing in every part of my life. I worked, I went to school, I dealt with people. I wasn’t walking around thinking everybody was plotting something.

This situation feels different to me because it’s specific. It’s tied to certain people and certain things that have happened. That’s why it bothers me when people try to make it sound like I’ve just always been suspicious, because I really don’t think that’s fair. I can be careful, sure, and I pay attention to details, especially with my kind of work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had some lifelong pattern of not trusting anyone.
